title: Package-config resolution tests silently pass when resources are missing
reasoning: Both bare-name resolution tests guard the resolver call and assertion with expected.exists(). If a required resource disappears or get_package_config_dir returns an incorrect directory, these tests complete successfully without exercising resolution. This hides failures in the exact resource-discovery behavior they are intended to protect.
reproduction: Run these two tests with their expected package resources absent. Both return without calling resolve_config_path or asserting any result.
recommendation: Remove the conditional guards and require the expected resources to exist before asserting bare-name resolution. If these are intended as isolated unit tests, provide a temporary package-config directory containing representative YAML and Jinja resources.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The assertions are conditional on successful resource discovery. The included missing-file tests verify errors for deliberately nonexistent names, not availability and resolution of bundled names.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand the existing bare-name scenarios to assert resource availability and successful resolution unconditionally for both configuration and prompt resources.
